blocks.md: Right now anyone who visits your app can see everything — there are no users, no accounts, no personal data. Authentication changes that. It is the gate that turns an anonymous visitor into a known person with their own id, their own rows in the database, and their own private data. Supabase does the hard part — hashing passwords, issuing tokens, refreshing sessions — so you can add real accounts in an afternoon.

blocks.canDo: add signup and login with Supabase Auth
blocks.md: By the end of this session you will be able to wire up Supabase Auth in a React app: build a signup form, build a login form using `supabase.auth.signInWithPassword(...)`, read the active session to know who is logged in, and get the logged-in user's `id` to attach to their database rows.

**Authentication = letting users prove who they are.**

Supabase Auth handles signup, login, and sessions for you. When a user signs up with email + password, Supabase stores a hashed credential and returns a **session** — a short-lived access token the client sends with every request. A session tells Supabase (and your app) *this request comes from user X*.

A logged-in user has a unique **`id`** (a UUID). You store that `id` as the `user_id` on every row that belongs to them — that is how you later query "show me only this user's data".

**v2 SDK method names:** older tutorials used `supabase.auth.signIn()` — that method is gone. The current v2 call is `supabase.auth.signInWithPassword({ email, password })`. Use `supabase.auth.signUp({ email, password })` to create an account and `supabase.auth.signOut()` to end the session.

**Keeping the UI in sync with login state:** call `supabase.auth.getSession()` once to read the current session, then subscribe with `supabase.auth.onAuthStateChange((event, session) => setSession(session))` inside a `useEffect` so your UI updates the moment someone logs in, logs out, or their token refreshes. Without this subscription your app won't react to login until a manual refresh.

### Primary reference — Supabase docs

Read the **"Password-based Auth"** guide in the Supabase docs. It covers creating an account with `signUp`, logging in with `signInWithPassword`, reading the active session, and signing out. Work through the code examples in your own project. Come back here when you have a working signup and login flow.

questions.question: What does authentication give each user that you attach to their database rows?
options: A username string you choose when creating the account
A unique UUID called `id` that identifies them across all their data
A row number auto-incremented by the database
An email-derived hash that serves as a primary key
questions.explanation: Supabase Auth gives every user a UUID `id`. You store that value as `user_id` on their rows so you can later query only their data.

questions.question: What is a session in Supabase Auth?
options: A browser tab that stays open while the user is active
A server-side database table that stores the user's current page
A short-lived access token returned after login that proves the user's identity on each request
A cookie that stores the user's password so they don't have to re-enter it
questions.explanation: A session is an access token (plus a refresh token) issued when the user logs in. The Supabase client attaches it automatically to every request, telling Supabase which user is making the call.

questions.question: Which is the correct Supabase v2 SDK call to log a user in with email and password?
questions.explanation: `signInWithPassword` is the v2 method. The old `signIn` was removed in the v2 SDK — using it will throw a runtime error.

blocks.md:
**What you covered:**

- Authentication lets users prove who they are; Supabase Auth handles hashing, tokens, and session refresh for you.
- Every logged-in user gets a UUID `id` — store it as `user_id` on their rows to scope queries to that user.
- A session is a short-lived access token the client sends automatically; reading `supabase.auth.getSession()` tells you whether someone is logged in.
- The v2 SDK renamed `signIn` to `signInWithPassword({ email, password })` — older tutorials use the old name.
